system-design-load-balancer-cdn-gateway..title: Three helpers at the front of a busy site
system-design-load-balancer-cdn-gateway..caption: The gateway checks every request, the load balancer shares the work between app copies, and the CDN keeps copies of files near the visitor so they arrive fast.
steps: Someone opens the site from their phone.
Pictures and style files come from a nearby copy, not from far away.
Checks the login and the limits, then picks the right service.
Sends the request to a server that is free.
It asks each server 'are you okay?' and skips the ones that fail.
Any copy can answer, because they do not remember visitors alone.
Logins and carts live in a shared place that every copy can read.
The visitor sees the page quickly, even on a busy day.

system-design-rate-limiter-token-bucket..title: The token bucket: fair turns for everyone
system-design-rate-limiter-token-bucket..caption: Every request spends a token. Tokens refill slowly. A quick burst is allowed, but nobody can take more than their fair share for long.
steps: It carries the user's id or key so we know whose bucket to use.
Each user has their own bucket, for example 10 tokens.
Spend one token and let the request through.
'Too many requests' plus a Retry-After hint: wait 5 seconds.
One new token arrives every second, up to the maximum.
A polite program waits for the time in the hint.
One noisy user cannot use up all the power.

system-design-search-inverted-index.svg.title: How search finds words fast
system-design-search-inverted-index.svg.caption: Instead of reading every note for each search, we build an index in advance, like the index in the back of a book. Then a search is just a quick lookup.
steps: 'The cat eats cat food' is saved in the database.
the, cat, eats, cat, food. Tiny words may be dropped.
cat gives 5 and 18. food gives 5 and 40.
Note 5 has both words, so it is the best match.
Best matches first. The index may be a moment behind.

system-design-cap-choice.svg.title: When the line between copies breaks
system-design-cap-choice.svg.caption: If two copies cannot talk, we must pick: stay correct and say 'wait', or keep answering and fix differences later. Pick by feature: money must be exact, likes can be a little old.
steps: Ana's notepad and Ben's notepad are kept the same by talking.
They cannot talk for a while. This is a partition.
'What is the score?' She cannot check with Ben.
'Please wait until I can confirm.' Safe, but no answer now.
'Last I knew it was 10.' Quick, but maybe old.
Choose A. A wrong answer here costs real money.
Choose B. A number that is a little old does no harm.
The copies compare notes and fix any conflicts.

system-design-consistent-hashing-ring.sv.title: A clock face for sharing data
system-design-consistent-hashing-ring.sv.caption: Machines and keys are placed on a circle. A key belongs to the first machine you meet clockwise. When a machine is added, only the keys next to it move, not everything.
steps: Think of a clock face with many tiny positions.
Machines A, B, and C are put at spots on the circle.
The key 'user42' becomes a number, which is a spot on the circle.
The first machine you reach stores that key.
It lands between A and B on the circle.
D takes only the keys between A and D. The rest stay.
With key modulo machines, nearly every key moves.
Each machine takes many spots, so the load is shared evenly.

system-design-url-shortener-flow.svg.title: Making and opening a short link
system-design-url-shortener-flow.svg.caption: Creating a link saves it in the database. Opening a link checks the cache first, because most traffic is opening, and then redirects the visitor to the long address.
steps: A user sends a very long web address.
The database gives the next number, for example 125.
125 in base62 becomes a short code like 'cb'. Longer in real life.
Save code and long link, and answer sho.rt/cb.
A popular code is answered straight from memory.
On a miss, read the database and fill the cache.
Reply 301 or 302: 'go to the long address'.

system-design-chat-message-flow.svg.title: How a chat message travels
system-design-chat-message-flow.svg.caption: The message is saved first so it is never lost. Online friends get it through their open connection. Offline friends get a push notification and fetch it when they return.
steps: Her phone sends it over an open connection.
It gives the message number 7 in this conversation.
The message is written to the database. Now it is safe.
One tick appears on Ana's screen.
The server looks up which server holds Ben's connection.
The message goes through the open connection right away.
A notification job goes to a worker and the phone buzzes.
Ben's phone confirms, and Ana sees two ticks.
